gen_risks.description: Armed conflict, ongoing regional violence, and mass population displacement across Central Africa may disrupt health service delivery and project operations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare, consult upon, disclose, and implement Security Risk Assessments (SRAs) and Security Management Plans (SMPs) tailored to fragile and conflict contexts.
gen_risks.evidence: Fragility in AFW is exacerbated by conflict and violence, leading to large population displacements... Boko Haram attacks in Cameroon and ongoing unrest in CAR

gen_risks.description: Challenging macro-fiscal conditions, high national debt burdens, and low domestic health expenditure threaten the long-term financial sustainability of health security investments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance to prepare Medium-Term Expenditure Frameworks, enhance domestic resource mobilization, and introduce budget tracking for health security.
gen_risks.evidence: A challenging macro-fiscal outlook... low government funding... The country's high debt burden limits public investment in health

gen_risks.description: Project implementation involving decentralized activities, workshops, and local capacity building presents financial management risks regarding questionable expenditures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Customize project accounting software, update financial procedures manuals, strengthen internal audit oversight, and recruit independent external auditors across implementing agencies.
gen_risks.evidence: several activities under the project like workshops, trainings and the local-level capacity building are at risk to generate questionable expenditures

gen_risks.description: Fragmented or uncoordinated cross-border mechanisms among CEMAC, WAHO, and participating national governments could hinder rapid disease surveillance and outbreak response.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish formal collaboration protocols through the Regional Coordination Committee (RCC), sign cross-border information-sharing agreements, and harmonize regional operational guides.
gen_risks.evidence: Disease outbreaks often cross borders, making coordinated cross-border collaboration essential, as fragmented efforts hinder effective response.

gen_risks.description: Weak institutional and procurement capacities in fragile country contexts could cause procurement delays, governance issues, and weak contract management.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish dedicated Project Implementation Units with qualified procurement specialists, deploy hands-on World Bank supervision, and apply flexible procurement arrangements.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement Risks include delays, governance issues, weak contract management, and limited market competition in fragile settings.

gen_risks.description: Increased deployment of frontline project workers and community health personnel poses substantial risks of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH).
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and implement SEA/SH Action Plans, recruit dedicated gender-based violence specialists, enforce codes of conduct, and establish accessible grievance mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: The overall project SEA/SH risks are judged to be substantial... increased presence of new health workforce... may create concerns of Sexual exploitation

gen_risks.description: Inadequate stakeholder engagement may result in the exclusion of vulnerable, displaced, or marginalized populations from health security planning and emergency services.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adapt Stakeholder Engagement Plans (SEPs) to country contexts, implement inclusive Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) strategies, and establish functional local GRMs.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential social risks are substantial and relate to: (i) inadequate stakeholder engagement... (ii) the exclusion of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups

gen_risks.description: Major public health emergencies and disease outbreaks may disrupt routine primary healthcare services, causing knock-on drops in essential care utilization.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and update facility-level contingency plans, establish epidemic-ready primary healthcare networks, and routinely monitor essential service delivery indicators.
gen_risks.evidence: Prior epidemics show that future health emergencies could further strain health systems... interruptions in the health sector induce further knock-on effects

gen_risks.description: Extreme climate events like severe flooding and droughts could damage healthcare infrastructure and accelerate outbreaks of vector- and water-borne diseases.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply green and resilient standards to facility refurbishments, integrate climate early warning systems into disease surveillance, and install solar power backup systems.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate change is a primary driver of health emergencies in Central Africa and already has negative impacts on health systems

gen_risks.description: The generation, handling, and disposal of hazardous healthcare waste and laboratory reagents pose risks to occupational health and community safety.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update and implement Healthcare Waste Management Plans, enforce biosafety and biosecurity protocols, and prepare site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plans.
gen_risks.evidence: laboratories will be supplied with reagents, chemicals, and equipment that may constitute medical waste once used.

gen_risks.description: High regional vulnerability to emerging zoonotic pathogens and increasing antimicrobial resistance (AMR) strains overburden existing diagnostic and surveillance systems.
gen_risks.mitigation: Operationalize One Health national action plans, establish regional laboratory networks with genomic sequencing capacity, and implement antimicrobial stewardship programs.
gen_risks.evidence: Central African countries face high vulnerability to infectious disease outbreaks... Zoonotic outbreaks... have risen... Central Africa is also significantly burdened by antimicrobial resistance

gen_risks.description: Gender disparities and systemic barriers severely restrict women's access to formal technical epidemiological and veterinary training and field roles.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement targeted female recruitment outreach, adopt flexible training formats, set explicit gender quotas for FETP and ISAVET courses, and monitor gender metrics.
gen_risks.evidence: women remain underrepresented in formal epidemiological training and decision-making... women dominate low-paid frontline roles but are largely absent from technical positions

gen_risks.description: Political instability and localized conflict in targeted areas (such as North-West and South-West Cameroon, CAR, or border zones) could physically restrict access to project sites.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt flexible implementation strategies in FCV areas, partner with local community actors, and enforce strict security management protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: Political instability, particularly in the North-West and South-West regions, may disrupt service delivery

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk (Moderate), considering fragility, socio-political instability, violence and weak governance of beneficiary countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close engagement by the World Bank to coordinate activities with other key partners.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk (Substantial), considering the complexities of coordinating national-level and regional-level activities to align and build on each other, and the different levels of readiness at country-level.
gt_risks.mitigation: Exploring the possibility of a coordinated implementation arrangement with CEMAC as the lead technical coordination body for regional activities.

gt_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability (Substantial), combined with overstretched or nonexistent PIUs in respective countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthening the existing PIUs and intensive capacity building and targeted TA for newly established PIUs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (Substantial) due to weak governance structures and inadequate FM systems.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on fiduciary processes.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk (Substantial) given the security risks associated with service delivery in FCV (fragility, conflict, and violence) settings.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on managing E&S risks.
